newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: OSCE calls for democratic reform in Yugoslavia.
newsitem.headline: OSCE calls for democratic reform in Yugoslavia.

text.p: Europe's top security watchdog gave a cautious welcome to the Yugoslav government's decision to recognise opposition wins in local polls and urged Belgrade to implement far-reaching democratic reforms.
In a statement released late on Wednesday, the Vienna-based OSCE repeated its call for talks between the government of President Slobodan Milosevic and opposition groups.

"The decision (to recognize the poll results) is hopefully a step towards positive democratic development in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The installation in office of the elected candidates is expected without delay," the OSCE chairman, Danish Foreign Minister Niels Helveg Petersen, said.
Milosevic climbed down over the disputed elections in 14 towns and cities on Tuesday after 11 weeks of mass protests. In November he had annulled the results, citing unspecified "irregularities".

"The Chairman-in-Office reiterates that the only way ahead is early democratic reform in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. A constructive dialogue on this issue between the government and opposition is needed," Petersen concluded.
